chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Isma'il ibn Mahbub, from Hanan ibn Sadir, who said: A man from the companions of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) narrated to me, saying: I heard him say:

The severest punishment on the Day of Resurrection will befall seven people: first, the son of Adam who killed his brother; and Nimrod who disputed with Ibrahim regarding his Lord; and two from the Children of Israel who made their communities Jewish and Christian; and Pharaoh who said, 'I am your lord, the Most High'; and two from this Ummah, one of whom is worse than the other. They will be kept in a casket of glass beneath the cleaving, in seas of fire.
ai.seo_question: Who are the seven people who will receive the severest punishment on the Day of Resurrection according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies seven archetypal figures whose sins serve as eternal warnings, ranging from Habil, the first murderer, to Pharaoh, who claimed divinity. Notably, the inclusion of two from the Bani Israel who solidified the distinct identities of Judaism and Christianity highlights the Shia scholarly view of their role in deviating from pure monotheism. The description of the worst among the Muslim Ummah as being encased in glass within seas of fire underscores the severity of internal corruption within the community.
